Summary: User Accounts & Profiles
Description: Deliver secure account access and a useful profile showing points balance and activity history.

Summary: Year-Round Activity Calendars
Description: Enable users to browse specialised year-round calendars, open daily doors, and read activity instructions.

Summary: Main Randomizer Calendar
Description: Provide the free-tier random activity draw with server-enforced cooldowns and anti-farming restrictions.

Summary: Points & Gamification Ledger
Description: Award points for eligible activity completions through a reliable ledger that prevents duplicate rewards.

Summary: Rewards Shop & Partner Offers
Description: Allow users to browse partner offers and redeem rewards using safe point checks, atomic deductions, and promo-code issuance.

Summary: Social Participation
Description: Support discovering, creating, and joining group activity sessions.

Summary: Subscription & Tier Access Control
Description: Enforce Free and Premium entitlements across calendars and rewards, including a functional Demo Tier Switcher.

Summary: QA, Presentation & Handover
Description: Validate the end-to-end product and its motivation hypothesis, then complete the presentation and formal handover by the deadline.

Summary: Register and log in securely
Description: As a visitor, I want to create an account and log in with valid credentials, so that I can access and retain my own platform experience. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) Registration validates required fields and rejects an already registered email 2) Passwords are stored using a secure one-way hash and login returns an authenticated session or token 3) Invalid credentials and malformed inputs return clear errors without exposing sensitive information || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (account rules and acceptance); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: View profile, points balance, and activity history
Description: As a signed-in user, I want to view my profile, current points balance, and completed activity history, so that I can understand my progress and earned rewards. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) Profile details and the current ledger-derived points balance are displayed for the signed-in account 2) Activity history lists completed activities with dates and points earned 3) A user cannot view or modify another user's profile or history || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (profile and history rules); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Browse specialised calendars and open daily doors
Description: As a calendar user, I want to browse Football, Fitness, and Mindfulness or Self-Help calendars and open available daily doors, so that I can find structured activities and understand how to complete them. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) The calendar catalogue displays the seeded calendar categories and indicates Free or Premium access 2) A user can open an available day and see its activity title, instructions, and completion guidance 3) Unavailable or locked days show a clear state and cannot be opened through a direct URL or API bypass || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (calendar rules and content); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Draw a free-tier random activity
Description: As a Free-tier user, I want to draw a random activity from the main calendar subject to a cooldown, so that I can discover a new activity without farming repeated draws. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) A draw selects an eligible activity from the configured free activity pool 2) The server enforces the configured cooldown and returns the next eligible draw time 3) Repeated requests during cooldown do not reveal another activity or bypass the restriction by refreshing or calling the API directly || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (pool and cooldown rules); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Complete activities and earn points once
Description: As a signed-in user, I want to mark an eligible activity complete and receive points in my ledger, so that I can track progress and earn rewards fairly. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) A valid completion creates a ledger entry and awards the configured points exactly once 2) Repeated completion submissions for the same user and activity do not create additional points 3) The updated balance and completion record are reflected in the profile and activity history || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (points and eligibility rules); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Browse and redeem partner rewards
Description: As a signed-in user, I want to browse partner offers and redeem a reward when I have enough points, so that I can exchange earned points for a usable partner offer. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) Each reward shows its description, point cost, availability, and relevant terms 2) Insufficient balances are rejected without deducting points or issuing a code 3) A successful redemption atomically deducts points and issues one valid promo code; concurrent duplicate requests cannot spend the same points twice || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (offer, price, and redemption rules); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Discover, create, and join group activity sessions
Description: As a signed-in user, I want to discover group sessions and create or join a session, so that I can participate in activities with other users. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) The session list displays available sessions with activity, host, date or time, and capacity where configured 2) A signed-in user can create a session with required details and valid capacity 3) Joining a session updates membership once and prevents duplicate joins or joining a full or closed session || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (session rules and UAT); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Enforce Free and Premium access with a Demo Tier Switcher
Description: As a demo user, I want to switch between Free and Premium demo tiers and see the corresponding access, so that I can verify subscription rules without a live payment integration. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) The Demo Tier Switcher changes the active demo tier and the UI visibly reflects the selected tier 2) Free users are restricted from configured Premium calendars and reward features while permitted Free features remain usable 3) Backend authorization enforces the same tier rules as the UI and rejects direct unauthorized requests || Contributors: Nizar (implementation); Youssef (entitlement matrix); Dhrruv (coordination)

Summary: Validate release quality and the Advent Calendar experience
Description: As a product owner, I want to validate the key user journeys, edge cases, and the motivational experience, so that the team can make an evidence-based release decision and explain the product's value. || Acceptance Criteria: 1) UAT covers registration, calendar discovery, daily-door activity, random draw, completion, points, rewards, and social participation 2) Duplicate completion, insufficient points, concurrent redemption, and unauthorized API scenarios have recorded expected results and outcomes 3) A small structured comparison captures user feedback on the Advent Calendar format versus a standard self-help activity list, with limitations clearly stated || Contributors: Youssef (UAT and product validation); Nizar (technical fixes and security evidence); Dhrruv (release coordination)

Summary: Implement registration and login backend
Description: Build the account data model and registration/login endpoints; hash passwords; validate input; issue and verify authenticated sessions or tokens; return safe error responses.

Summary: Build registration and login frontend
Description: Implement registration and login screens, field validation, loading and error states, and authenticated navigation using the agreed API contract.

Summary: Implement profile and activity-history API
Description: Create authenticated endpoints for the current user's profile, ledger-derived points balance, and paginated or bounded activity history; enforce account ownership.

Summary: Build profile dashboard UI
Description: Display profile information, current points, and recent completed activities; include loading, empty, and error states.

Summary: Implement calendar data model and APIs
Description: Create or adapt calendar, day, and activity data structures and endpoints for calendar catalogue, calendar detail, daily-door availability, and activity instructions.

Summary: Build calendar browsing and daily-door UI
Description: Implement specialised calendar catalogue, Free or Premium indicators, daily-door states, and activity instruction view with clear locked and unavailable states.

Summary: Implement random draw API and cooldown enforcement
Description: Build the server-side eligible-activity draw and persist or derive the cooldown so repeated requests, refreshes, and direct API calls cannot bypass it.

Summary: Build main randomizer UI
Description: Implement the free-tier random draw interaction, activity result, cooldown countdown or next-available state, and clear restriction messaging.

Summary: Implement transactional points ledger and duplicate prevention
Description: Create the points ledger and completion transaction so eligible activity points are awarded once; enforce a unique completion or idempotency constraint and keep the balance consistent.

Summary: Integrate activity completion UI with points history
Description: Connect the completion action to the API and show success, duplicate-completion, and updated-points states without optimistic double-awards.

Summary: Implement rewards catalogue API
Description: Create reward and partner-offer data structures and endpoints exposing active offers, point cost, terms, and availability without exposing private promo codes prematurely.

Summary: Implement atomic reward redemption and promo issuance
Description: Validate the current balance and reward stock inside a transaction; deduct points and reserve or issue one promo code atomically; make repeated or concurrent requests safe.

Summary: Build rewards shop and redemption UI
Description: Implement offer cards, point-sufficiency feedback, redemption confirmation, insufficient-points messaging, and display of the issued promo code after success.

Summary: Implement group session data model and API
Description: Create session and membership data structures plus authenticated endpoints to discover, create, and join sessions; validate capacity, status, and duplicate membership.

Summary: Build group session discovery and participation UI
Description: Implement session discovery, create-session form, session details, and join flow with full, closed, and already-joined states.

Summary: Implement tier entitlement checks in backend
Description: Implement a central Free/Premium entitlement rule and enforce it on calendar and reward APIs; ensure UI-only tier changes cannot bypass server-side access control.

Summary: Build functional Demo Tier Switcher
Description: Add a demo-only tier switcher and connect it to visible access states for calendars and rewards; make clear that it simulates subscription status and does not process payments.

Summary: Run technical security and API smoke tests
Description: Test missing or invalid authentication, cross-user data access, locked Premium endpoints, malformed inputs, duplicate completion requests, insufficient-point redemption, and concurrent redemption; fix release-blocking defects.

Summary: Prepare technical documentation and deployment runbook
Description: Document architecture and key API contracts, environment configuration, database setup or migrations, seed procedure, local run instructions, demo credentials handling, known limitations, and deployment or rollback steps.

Summary: Define product rules and entitlement matrix
Description: Agree and record points per completion, eligible completion conditions, randomizer cooldown, Free versus Premium calendar and reward access, session capacity rules, reward point costs, and redemption limits; turn decisions into testable examples.

Summary: Prepare and seed specialised calendar content
Description: Prepare and enter demo-ready Football, Fitness, and Mindfulness or Self-Help calendars with day titles, concise instructions, tier designation, and enough activities to demonstrate browsing and daily doors end to end.

Summary: Seed partner offers and demo promo codes
Description: Prepare realistic demo partner rewards, point prices, terms, availability, and a controlled promo-code pool; verify that the seeded data supports successful and insufficient-points redemption demos.

Summary: Prepare UAT checklist and test data
Description: Create concise end-to-end UAT steps, expected outcomes, test accounts for Free and Premium demo tiers, sample activity completions, reward balances, and group sessions.

Summary: Execute UAT and record edge-case results
Description: Run the agreed user journeys and explicitly verify duplicate completion, insufficient points, concurrent redemption attempts, and unauthorized API access; log defects with severity, evidence, owner, and retest result.

Summary: Validate Advent Calendar motivation hypothesis
Description: Run a small structured feedback comparison using the Advent Calendar experience and a standard self-help activity-list baseline; capture perceived motivation, likelihood to return, and qualitative comments, and state the small-sample limitation in the presentation.

Summary: Complete Product Owner acceptance and sign-off
Description: Review acceptance criteria, UAT outcomes, known limitations, and release-blocking defects; record accepted scope and provide final Product Owner sign-off by the handover deadline.

Summary: Coordinate sprint plan, Jira board, and daily tracking
Description: Maintain the prioritized board, confirm owners and due dates, run short daily check-ins, track blockers and scope changes, and escalate any risk to the 12 November presentation and handover deadline.

Summary: Prepare final presentation and product narrative
Description: Create the presentation covering problem, target users, product concept, key journeys, architecture, gamification and tier rules, demo results, motivation comparison, limitations, and next steps.

Summary: Prepare end-to-end demo script and rehearsal
Description: Write a timed demo walkthrough covering registration, calendar door, randomizer cooldown, completion and points, reward redemption, social session, and Free/Premium tier switching; rehearse and prepare a fallback path.

Summary: Assemble formal handover package
Description: Compile final backlog status, scope delivered, architecture overview, setup and run instructions, links to technical documentation, test evidence, known issues, access or ownership notes, and recommended next steps for the receiving team.
